construction_markdown: No new leaderboard code is claimed. Three finite conclusions were proved: the shared dimension-1040 RS–affine construction is maximal among additive outer supercodes using its fixed affine inner encoder; the proposed `[8192,17,4090]_2` inner constituent does not exist; and degree-at-most-five Delsarte certificates cannot settle the remaining `[32768,18,16381]_2` constituent question.

Hence `A_2(8192,4090)<=116581<2^17`. This closes the optimized `[131072,65,131008]_{2^17}` concatenation route of dimension `1105`, not merely the earlier dimension-1054 specialization.

Thus no strict additive outer supercode containing the degree-at-most-64 RS space works with the fixed affine-RM inner map. proof_markdown:
# Finite obstruction note

Set `n=2^30` and `D=535822336`.

## 1. Additive maximality of the fixed RS–affine architecture

Let

`F=F_2[theta]/(theta^16+theta^5+theta^3+theta^2+1)`,

`A=span_F2{1,theta,...,theta^14}`,

and let `D_0` be evaluation on `A` of all polynomials of degree at most 64. For `z=sum z_i theta^i`, define

`H(z)_y=z_0+sum_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i`,  `y in F_2^15`.

For `v in F^A`, put `Delta(v)=N_0(v)-N_1(v)`. The blocks `H(0)`, `H(1)`, and `H(z)` for `z notin {0,1}` have weights `0`, `2^15`, and `2^14`, respectively. Hence

`wt(H^A(v))=2^14(32768-Delta(v))`.

Because `D=2^14(32768-64)`, the target is exactly `Delta(v)<=64` for every nonzero outer word.

Suppose that an `F_2`-linear space `V` strictly contains `D_0` and that `H^A(V)` meets the target. Choose `g in V\D_0`. Fix any 64-set `R subset A`, let `q_R` be the degree-at-most-63 interpolant agreeing with `g` on `R`, and put

`G_R(X)=product_{r in R}(X-r)`.

For every `lambda in F`, define

`u_lambda=g+ev_A(q_R+lambda G_R)`.

These vectors lie in `V`, vanish on `R`, and are nonzero; otherwise `g` would belong to `D_0`. At each `a notin R`, the value `u_lambda(a)` runs bijectively through `F` as `lambda` varies. Therefore the average of `Delta(u_lambda)` over `lambda` is 64. Since every term is at most 64, all terms equal 64.

For `a notin R`, set

`x_a=(g(a)+q_R(a))/G_R(a)` and `c_a=1/G_R(a)`.

Zeros outside `R` occur at parameters `lambda=x_a`, while ones occur at `lambda=x_a+c_a`. Equality `Delta(u_lambda)=64` for every parameter means that the multisets `{x_a}` and `{x_a+c_a}` have identical multiplicities. Summing their elements in `F` gives the necessary condition

`sum_{a in A\R} 1/G_R(a)=0`.  (1)

Now take

`U=span_F2{1,theta,...,theta^5}={0x0000,...,0x003f}`,

`b=theta^6=0x0040`, and `R=(U\{0}) union {b}`.

The subspace polynomial `P(X)=product_{u in U}(X-u)`, obtained from `P_{V+<v>}=P_V^2+P_V(v)P_V`, is

`P(X)=X^64+0x2e0c X^32+0x71ee X^16+0xd9a4 X^8+0x2198 X^4+0xc6ca X^2+0x6115 X`.

Write `c_0=0x6115`, `c_1=0xc6ca`, and `beta=P(b)=0xe9f1`. Since

`G_R(X)=P(X)(X-b)/X`,

grouping `A\U` into the 64-element fibers of the additive map `P:A->P(A)` gives

`sum_{a in A\R}1/G_R(a)=1/(c_0b)+1/beta+b c_1/(c_0 beta)`.  (2)

Indeed, `a=0` supplies the first term. The complete nonzero `P`-fibers cancel in the sum of `1/P(a)`, except that deleting `b` leaves `1/beta`. For the second summand in

`1/G_R(a)=1/P(a)+b/[P(a)(a+b)]`,

the `beta`-fiber gives `c_1/(c_0 beta)` because `sum_{u in U\{0}}u^{-1}=c_1/c_0`; all other fibers cancel in pairs `y,y+beta`.

Exact reduction modulo the defining polynomial gives

`1/(c_0b)=0xac5c`, `1/beta=0x073e`, `b c_1/(c_0 beta)=0xa2f2`.

Their sum is `0x0990`, contradicting (1). Thus `V=D_0`: the fixed-inner construction has no strict additive outer extension.

## 2. Cubic Delsarte exclusion of `[8192,17,4090]_2`

For a binary code `X` of size `M`, let

`A_i=M^{-1}|{(x,y) in X^2 : d(x,y)=i}|`.

Then `A_0=1`, `sum_i A_i=M`, and character orthogonality gives

`sum_i A_i K_j(i)=M^{-1} sum_{|S|=j}|sum_{x in X}(-1)^{sum_{r in S}x_r}|^2>=0`.  (3)

Take `n_0=8192`, `d_0=4090`, and `t=n_0-2i`. Every occurring nonzero distance has even `t` with `-8192<=t<=12`. Define

`p(t)=(t-12)(t+630)(t+632)`.

Its only positive real interval below 12 is `(-632,-630)`, which contains no even integer. Hence `p(t)<=0` at every allowed nonzero distance. With

`K_0=1`, `K_1=t`, `K_2=(t^2-n_0)/2`,

`K_3=(t^3-(3n_0-2)t)/6`,

the exact expansion is

`p=5462080K_0+407590K_1+2500K_2+6K_3`.

All coefficients are nonnegative. Equation (3) therefore gives

`5462080 M <= sum_i A_i p(n_0-2i) <= p(n_0)`.

Finally,

`p(8192)=636774783040`,

so

`M<=636774783040/5462080=116581+34560/5462080<116582`.

Thus `A_2(8192,4090)<=116581<131072=2^17`, excluding even nonlinear codes of the required size.

## 3. Exact product ledger and the next LP boundary

Had the excluded inner code existed, the optimal full-length outer RS parameters would have been

`[131072,65,131008]_{2^17}`,

giving final dimension `17*65=1105` and product distance `4090*131008=535822720`.

The largest currently isolated surviving product gateway is `[16384,16,8185]_2`: the corresponding full-length outer code is `[65536,73,65464]_{2^16}`, giving conditional dimension 1168 and distance 535822840.

For `[32768,18,16381]_2`, degree-at-most-five Delsarte LP is provably insufficient. Put `M=2^18` and define the fractional distance distribution

`A_0=1`, `A_16381=26180051/100`, `A_18725=34249/100`,

with all other entries zero. It is nonnegative and sums to `M`. If `P_j(t)=j!K_j(i)` for `t=32768-2i`, then

`P_0=1`, `P_1=t`, `P_{j+1}=tP_j-j(32768-j+1)P_{j-1}`.

The transforms for `j=1,...,5` are respectively

`3288/100`, `99780912/100`, `3306612305808/100`,

`131665556518733670720/100`, and

`3700836372238323167357760/100`,

all positive. Weak duality therefore prevents any degree-at-most-five nonnegative-Krawtchouk certificate from forcing cardinality below `2^18`. This fractional distribution is only a proof-method obstruction, not a code.

## 4. Concurrent conditional-average proposal

The arithmetic, Fourier normalization, circuit enumeration, expurgation, dimension, and distance arguments in the concurrent dimension-2971 proposal were independently checked and are mathematically consistent. Its generator, however, is selected by comparing exact averages over every completion of each matrix prefix. No closed evaluator or structural pessimistic estimator is supplied.

This is materially an exhaustive numerical search: for any nonempty finite witness set `W`, applying the same rule to the failure indicator of `W` deterministically returns an element of `W`. Treating unrestricted completion averages as an explicit construction would therefore make every finite search nominally explicit, contrary to `CONTRIBUTOR_INSTRUCTIONS.md`. Consequently that proposal is not used as a leaderboard submission here.

proof_steps.proof: Affine character orthogonality gives block weights `0`, `2^15`, and `2^14` on symbols `0`, `1`, and all other symbols, respectively.
proof_steps.statement: The fixed affine-inner target is exactly `N_0-N_1<=64`.

proof_steps.proof: Interpolate an alleged new outer direction on 64 points and vary the coefficient of their root polynomial. Averaging forces equality in every pencil member, and equality of the zero- and one-parameter multisets forces the reciprocal sum to vanish.
proof_steps.statement: Every admissible strict extension would require `sum_{a in A\R}G_R(a)^(-1)=0` for every 64-set `R`.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed subspace polynomial and its fiber decomposition reduce the sum to three exact field elements whose sum is `0x0990`.
proof_steps.statement: The fixed set `R={0x0001,...,0x0040}` violates the necessary reciprocal identity.

proof_steps.proof: Any strict additive supercode contains a coset represented by `g` outside the RS space, contradicting the explicit reciprocal witness.
proof_steps.statement: The degree-at-most-64 RS outer space is inclusion-maximal under the fixed affine-RM inner encoder.

proof_steps.proof: The Krawtchouk transforms of a binary distance distribution are sums of squared character sums and hence nonnegative.
proof_steps.statement: The finite Delsarte inequality used in the cubic certificate holds for every binary code.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed cubic is nonpositive on every admissible even distance parameter, has four nonnegative Krawtchouk coefficients, and evaluates to the stated exact quotient.
Lengths and dimensions multiply under concatenation; the outer distances are the exact ceilings of the target divided by the proposed inner distances.
proof_steps.statement: The excluded route had optimized dimension 1105; the surviving 16-dimensional gateway would have optimized dimension 1168.

proof_steps.proof: The displayed nonnegative fractional distance distribution has total size `2^18`, support at allowed distances, and positive Krawtchouk transforms through degree five. Weak duality rules out a degree-at-most-five exclusion certificate.

The selector computes unrestricted averages over all completions. Applied to a failure indicator, the same rule selects a witness from every nonempty finite set, so it is a generic exhaustive numerical search rather than a structural construction.
proof_steps.statement: The concurrent dimension-2971 proposal needs a non-search selector or an explicit policy waiver before leaderboard acceptance.

theorem_statement: Let `D_0` be the degree-at-most-64 evaluation space underlying the shared dimension-1040 RS–affine code. Under its fixed coordinatewise affine-RM inner encoder, no strict `F_2`-additive outer supercode containing `D_0` meets the target. Independently, `A_2(8192,4090)<=116581`, so the optimized dimension-1105 product gateway is impossible. These are scoped obstructions and do not improve the leaderboard.
